# Mixdog

The open-source coding agent that uses 63% fewer tokens. 
 [**Download ↓**](<https://docs.example.com/README.md#installation>)

[https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af515dc9-b0fb-4b6a-aaa1-1d82db792ed0](<https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af515dc9-b0fb-4b6a-aaa1-1d82db792ed0>)

[![Download for Windows](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tribgames/mixdog/main/docs/assets/download-windows.svg>)](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-win-x64.exe>) [![Download for macOS](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tribgames/mixdog/main/docs/assets/download-macos.svg>)](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-mac-arm64.dmg>) [![Download for Linux](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tribgames/mixdog/main/docs/assets/download-linux.svg>)](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-linux-x86_64.AppImage>) 
 macOS button is for Apple Silicon (M1 and later). Intel Mac? [Download for Intel Mac](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-mac-x64.dmg>). Linux button is the x64 AppImage; .deb and ARM64 builds are listed below.

[![Release](<https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/tribgames/mixdog?style=flat-square>)](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest>) [![npm](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/mixdog?style=flat-square>)](<https://www.npmjs.com/package/mixdog>) [![License](<https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue?style=flat-square>)](<https://docs.example.com/LICENSE>) [![GitHub Sponsors](<https://img.shields.io/github/sponsors/JYP8877?style=flat-square&logo=githubsponsors&label=Sponsors>)](<https://github.com/sponsors/JYP8877>)

[**Website**](<https://mixdog.ai/>) · [**Benchmarks**](<https://docs.example.com/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2.1/>) · [**Docs**](<https://docs.example.com/README.md#documentation>)

## Highlights

- [63% fewer tokens](<https://docs.example.com/README.md#benchmarks>) than Codex CLI on the same model, at the same success rate.
- [**Auto reasoning effort**](<https://docs.example.com/docs/auto-reasoning-effort.md>) — each message and tool step gets the effort it needs, judged in about 0.1 s by a 150 MB model that runs locally on the CPU. On by default.
- Use the **Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, or Muse Code** subscription you already have, API keys, or local models on your own GPU.
- Mix models by role and scale from **Solo to Swarm** — a strong model leads while cheaper ones search, edit, and review in parallel. Switch the workflow or mode mid-conversation, and set fallback models for usage limits.
- **Bots and rooms** — your own bots with their own models, tools, and permissions, group rooms where they talk together, and a representative bot that sits above the composer on your desktop.
- A full workspace: editor, terminals, Git and GitHub, code graph, and language servers, with themes and photo skins.
- Keeps working on its own with **Goals, schedules, and webhooks** — and continues from your phone, end-to-end encrypted.
- Goes beyond code with **browser and desktop control**, Office and PDF documents, and image and video generation.
- Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. No config files.

## Installation

Download the desktop app:

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| Windows (x64) | [` mixdog-desktop-win-x64.exe `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-win-x64.exe>) |
| macOS (Apple Silicon) | [` mixdog-desktop-mac-arm64.dmg `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-mac-arm64.dmg>) |
| macOS (Intel) | [` mixdog-desktop-mac-x64.dmg `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-mac-x64.dmg>) |
| Linux (x64, AppImage) | [` mixdog-desktop-linux-x86_64.AppImage `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-linux-x86_64.AppImage>) |
| Linux (x64, .deb) | [` mixdog-desktop-linux-amd64.deb `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-linux-amd64.deb>) |
| Linux (ARM64, AppImage) | [` mixdog-desktop-linux-arm64.AppImage `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-linux-arm64.AppImage>) |
| Linux (ARM64, .deb) | [` mixdog-desktop-linux-arm64.deb `](<https://github.com/tribgames/mixdog/releases/latest/download/mixdog-desktop-linux-arm64.deb>) |

Then sign in with a ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, or Muse Code account, or paste an API key. A five-step tutorial walks you through the rest.

> \[!NOTE\] The Windows installer and app are code-signed, and the Mac app is signed and notarized. If SmartScreen still appears, choose **More info → Run anyway**.

Or run it in the terminal (Node.js 22.19+ or 24+):

```bash
npm install -g mixdog
mixdog
```

  Supported providers 

- Anthropic API keys and Claude account OAuth
- OpenAI API keys and ChatGPT/Codex account OAuth
- Google Gemini API keys
- xAI API keys and Grok account OAuth
- Muse Code (Meta) account OAuth
- OpenRouter, DeepSeek, and OpenCode Go
- Built-in **Local Provider** — download and run models in the app (Windows x64 with an NVIDIA GPU)

Cursor, Antigravity (Gemini), and MiMo OAuth are off by default under **Settings → Developer**; using them through OAuth risks account restrictions.

   Headless ` mixdog exec ` 

` mixdog exec ` runs one non-interactive, single-model session without personal memory, prior sessions, skills, MCP servers, or plugins:

```bash
mixdog exec --provider openai-oauth --model gpt-5.6-sol --effort xhigh "fix the failing test"
```

Web search is off by default (` --web-search ` enables it). This does not block shell networking — headless exec is not an offline sandbox. Run ` mixdog --help ` for the full reference.

## Benchmarks

![Bar chart: Mixdog vs Codex CLI on Terminal-Bench 2.1](<https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tribgames/mixdog/main/design/promo/tb21-sol-vs-codex-light.svg>)

*All 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks × 5 trials on GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh, scored by the official Harbor verifier.*

Mixdog used fewer tokens on 87 of 89 tasks. With Claude Opus 5, it solved 2 more tasks than Claude Code at 19% lower cost. Every verdict, log, and script is published in [` benchmarks/terminal-bench-2.1/ `](<https://docs.example.com/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2.1/>), and [Context efficiency](<https://docs.example.com/docs/context-efficiency.md>) explains where the savings come from.

  **Benchmark history** 

Newest first. Each run links to its details, records, and caveats.

| Run | Model · trials | vs | Score | Cost | Final context | Time / trial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2026-10-15](<https://docs.example.com/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2.1/#bench-log>) | GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh · ` k=1 ` | Codex CLI | 77 vs 78 /89 | **−55%** | **−68%** (10.8K vs 33.6K) | 344s vs 380s |
| [2026-08-25](<https://docs.example.com/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2.1/#gpt-56-sol-xhigh-vs-codex-cli>) | GPT-5.6 Sol xhigh · ` k=5 ` | Codex CLI | 385 vs 383 /445 | **−39%** | **−46%** (18.5K vs 34.3K) | 415s vs 437s |
| [2026-08-25](<https://docs.example.com/benchmarks/terminal-bench-2.1/#claude-opus-5-vs-claude-code>) | Claude Opus 5 · ` k=1 ` | Claude Code | 79 vs 77 /89 | **−19%** | **−28%** (27.6K vs 38.2K) | 610s vs 708s |

The 2026-10-15 run is the first full run with the [effort judge](<https://docs.example.com/docs/auto-reasoning-effort.md>) active on OpenAI routes, with web search on for both sides. It is a single pass, so the ` k=5 ` chart above stays the reference.
